workingTitle: A young star and its debris disk are tilted apart
coreFacts: JWST/NIRCam obtained the first scattered-light images of the 24-million-year-old CPD-72 2713 debris disk in the F210M and F444W filters.
Forward modeling measured characteristic scattered-light radii of 55.4 +3.0/-3.2 AU and 39.1 +4.6/-2.6 AU.
The minimum star-disk mutual tilt is about 27 degrees, and exceeds 10 degrees at 95% credibility in both filters.
JWST rules out planets heavier than about 0.3 Jupiter masses beyond 0.5 arcseconds, weakening a massive-planet explanation for the tilt.
Published disk inclination differences and other systematic uncertainties could affect the inferred misalignment probability.

sources.label: Zhang et al., accepted by The Astrophysical Journal
